and al-Husayn (peace be on them); and he (the Messenger of God) said about ʿAlī: ‘Whoever’s master am I, ʿAlī is his master.’ Also the Messenger of God said: ‘I admonish you concerning the Book of God and my Ahl al-bayt; verily I have asked God not to let them be separated from each other until He brings them to the hawd (reservoir [of al-Kawthar]), and He has granted it to me.’ And he said: ‘Do not teach them because they are more knowledgeable than you; verily they shall never take you away from the gate of guidance and shall never let you enter the gate of misguidance.’ If the Messenger of God had remained silent and not identified the people (of his Ahl al-bayt), surely the progeny of ʿAbbās, and the progeny of ʿAqīl and someone else’s progeny would have claimed (to be among them); but God revealed in His Book: Allah only desires to keep away the uncleanness from you, O people of the House! and to purify you a (thorough) purification [33:33]; and ʿAlī and al-Hasan and al-Husayn and Fātimah

(peace be on them) were the interpretation of this verse; so the Messenger of God took the hands of ʿAlī and Fātimah and alHasan and al-Husayn (blessings from God be upon them) and entered them under the mantle in the house of Umm Salamah and said: ‘O God! every prophet had his precious things and his people; and these are my precious things and my people’ Umm Salamah said: ‘Am I not from your people?’ He said: ‘Verily you are (preceding) to good but these are my precious things and people of my (house).’. (al-Tafsīr, al-ʿAyyāshī)

Author’s comments: al-Kulaynī has narrated in al-Kāf , through his chain of narrators from Abū Basīr from the same Imām a similar tradition with minor differences in wordings.

(9) Ibn Shahrāshūb has quoted from al-Tafsīr of Mujāhid that this verse [of obedience] was revealed about the Leader of the faithful [ʿAlī] when the Messenger of God lefiihim in Medina as his

deputy. (ʿAlī) said: ‘‘O Messenger of God! Are you leaving me to look after the women and the children?’’ He [the Messenger of God] said: ‘‘O Leader of the faithful! Are you not pleased that you should have the same position with me as Aaron had with Moses, when (Moses) said to him: ‘Take my place among my people, and act well’? Then God said: ‘and those vested with authority from among you’.’’ (The Imām then) said: ‘‘ ʿAlī b. Abī Tālib, God appointed him as the master of the ummah’s affairs after Muḥammad and when the Messenger of God made him take his place at Medina. Thus God ordered the servants to obey him (ʿAlī) and not to go against him.’’ (Tafsīr al-Burhān).

Mujāhid has also narrated from Ibānah al-Falakī that it was revealed when Abū Buraydah complained against ʿAlī (ibid.)

(10) A tradition has been quoted in ʿAbaqāt al-anwār from Yanābīʿ al-mawaddah of al-Shaykh Sulaymān b. Ibrāhīm al-Balkhī who quotes from al Manāqib, from Sulaym b. Qays al-Hilālī from ʿAlī which, inter alia, says: [ʿAlī] said, ‘‘The least by which a servant goes astray is that he does not know the Proof of God, the Blessed, the Sublime, and His witness over His servants, whose obedience God has ordered and whose love and obedience made obligatory.’’

Sulaym says, ‘‘I said, ‘O Leader of the faithful! describe them to me.’ He said, ‘(They are) those whom God has joined with Himself and His Messenger, and said: O you who believe! obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those vested with authority from among you.’ I said to him, ‘May God make me your ransom! explain (it)

to me.’ He said, ‘Those (about whom) the Messenger of God had said in several places and his last sermon on the day when God, the Mighty, the Great, took him to Himself: ‘‘Surely I am leaving among you two things, you shall never go astray after me if you hold fast to them: the Book of God, the Mighty, the Great, and my progeny who are my Ahl al-bayt; because [God,] the Kind, the Knower, has promised me that they shall never be separated (from each other) until they come to me at the Reservoir—like these two (saying this, the Prophet joined his index fingers together) and I do not say ‘like these two’ (saying which he joined his index and middle fingers together); so hold fast to them both and don’t go ahead of them, otherwise you would go astray.’’ ’ ’’ Author’s comments: Traditions narrated from the Imāms of Ahl al-bayt, giving similar meanings as above are very numerous. What we have presented here gives examples of all types of meanings described in traditions. Anyone wanting more details should consult collections of traditions.

As for ancient exegetes, they are divided about the meaning of the phrase, ulu al-amr. Some say, it means the rightly guided caliphs; others say, commanders of expeditions; a third group says, the scholars.

al-Dahhāk has reportedly said that it refers to the companions of the Prophet; but it boils down to the third interpretation, because reportedly he has said: ‘‘They are companions of the Messenger of God as they were the callers (to Islam) and narrators of traditions.’, Obviously, this reasoning is based on their knowledge, and this interpretation would ultimately

mean the scholars.

It should be noted that many things and various stories have been reported concerning the reason of revelation of this verse; but if one ponders on them one would be in no doubt that all of them are mere attempts by the narrators to apply the verse on one or the other view or situation. We therefore have not quoted any of them as it was of no value. You may look into al-Durr al-Manthūr and al-Tafsīr of al-Ṭabarī and other books like them for verification of this observation.

(11) al-Barqī has narrated through his chain from Abu al-Jārūd that Abū Jaʿfar said about the verse, But no! by your Lord! they do not believe until they ... submit with total submission: ‘‘Submission is pleasure and satisfaction with His decree.’’ (al-Mahāsin)

(12) ʿAbdullāh al-Kāhilī has said that Abū ʿAbdillāh said: ‘‘If a people worshipped God alone who has no partner, and established

prayer, and gave zakāt, and performed hajj of the House, and fasted in the month of Ramadān, and then said about a thing done by God or by His Messenger, ‘Why did he do this?’ Or, ‘If he had done it in another way [it would have been better]’ or felt [annoyance] in their hearts, they would become polytheists because of it.’’ Then he recited this verse, But no! by your Lord! they do not believe until they make you a judge of that which has become a matter of disagreement among them, and then do not find any straitness in their hearts as to what you have decided and submit with total submission. Then Abū ʿAbdillāh said: ‘‘It is incumbent upon you to submit.’’ (al-Kāf )

(13) ʿAbdullāh b. Yahyā al-Kāhilī has narrated that he heard Abū ʿAbdillāh saying: ‘‘By God, if a people worshipped God alone who has no partner, and established prayer, and gave zakāt, and performed hajj of the House, and fasted in the month of Ramadān, and then said about a thing done of the Messenger of God, ‘Why did he do this or that? or felt [annoyance] in their hearts, they would become polytheists because of it.’’ Then he recited, But no! by your Lord! they do not believe until they make you a judge of that which has become a matter of disagreement among them, and then do not find any straitness in their hearts as to what—Muḥammad and the progeny of Muḥammad—have decided and submit with total submission. (al-Tafsīr, al-ʿAyyāshī). Author’s comments: There are other traditions similar to these two. The meaning given by the Imām extends the theme of the verse on two counts: First, that the verse covers all decisions and decrees, be they legislative or creative; Second, it makes no difference whether the decision

or decree was issued by God or by His Messenger.

It should be mentioned here that there are other traditions which apply the verse, But no! by your Lord! they ... submit with total submission,

to the wilayah of ʿAlī or the wilāyah of the Imāms of Ahl al-bayt; they provide examples of applying a verse to one or the other of its prominent models. Certainly the verse is applicable to God, His Messenger and the Imāms of Ahl al-bayt, and it continues in them.

(14) al-Shaykh has narrated through his chain from ʿAlī that he said: ‘‘A man from the Helpers (ansār) came to the Prophet and said:

‘O Messenger of God! I cannot bear separation from you; so much so that if I enter my home and remember you, I leave my property and come (here) for looking at you, in your love. Then I remembered that when the Day of Resurrection would come, you would be made to enter the Garden and raised to the highest level of ʿilliyyīn (highest place). Then how could I see you? O

Messenger of God!’ Then the verse was revealed: And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger, these are with those upon whom Allah has bestowed favors from among the prophets, and the truthful, and the witnesses, and the good ones; and excellent are these as

companion! Thereupon the Prophet sent for the man and recited it to him and gave him the good news.’’ (al-Amālī, al-Shaykh)

Author’s comments: This theme is also narrated through Sunnī chains in al-Durr al-Manthūr quoting from al-Ṭabarānī, Ibn Marduwayh, Abū Nuʿaym (in Hilyat al-awliyāʾ) and al-Diyāʾ al-Maqdisī (in Sifat al jannah, saying that this tradition was ‘good’), all narrating from ʿĀʾishah; also quoting from al-Ṭabarānī and Ibn Marduwayh both through al-Shaʿbī from Ibn ʿAbbās; and through Saʿīd b. Mansūr and Ibn al-Mundhir from al-Shaʿbī; and through Ibn Jarīr from Saʿīd b. Jubayr.

(15) Ibn Shahrāshūb has narrated from Anas b. Mālik from someone he had named from Abū Sālih from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said about this verse: ‘‘And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger, these are with those upon whom Allah has bestowed favors from among the prophets—that is, Muḥammad—and the truthful—that is, ʿAlī, and he was the first to verify—and the witnesses—that is, ʿAlī, Jaʿfar, Hamzah, al-Hasan and al-Husayn, peace be on them.’’1 (Tafsīr al-Burhān)

Author’s comments: There are other traditions giving the same meaning.

(16) al-Bāqir said: ‘‘Help us with piety, because whoever met God with piety, would get happiness near God, as God, the Mighty, the Great, says: And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger ...’’

After reciting the verse, he said: ‘‘So from us is the Prophet, and from us is the truthful, and from us are the witnesses and the good ones.’’ (al-Kāf )

(17) al-Sādiq has said: ‘‘The believers are of two kinds: (One is) a believer who fulfils the conditions God had imposed on him; he will be with the prophets, and the truthful, and the witnesses, and the good ones; and excellent are these as companions! and he is among those who will intercede and will not need intercession (by others); and he is among those who are not inflicted with terror of this world, nor of the hereafter. (Another is) a believer who has made mistakes. He is like a green stalk, which inclines

1 This tradition obviously interprets the word al-shuhadāʾ as martyrs, not witnesses. [Trans.]

to whichever direction wind pushes it and then returns to its position. He is among those who are inflicted with terrors of this world and that of the hereafter, and he would be interceded for;

and he is on good.’’ (ibid.)

Author’s comments: al-Sihāh says: ‘‘al-Khāmah is a green sofiiplant.’’ The Imām in this hadīth points to what was described in the Commentary of the verse, The path of those upon whom Thou hast bestowed favors

(1:7), that ‘favor’ means al-wilāyah (love, mastership, friendship). This explanation thus corresponds with the verses, Now surely the friends of Allah, they shall have no fear nor shall they grieve. Those who believed and were pious (10:62–63). Terror of mishaps cannot reach the friends of God who rely on none other than God.
